sections.title: Molecular profile of malignant ovarian germ cell tumours
sections.intro: MOGCT are **low-mutation, copy-number–driven** tumours. No biomarker selects a targeted or immunotherapy option; **AFP and β-hCG** drive risk and relapse detection. IT grade is the main relapse factor (no relapses in grade 1) [19]; YST is present in 91% of mixed MOGCT, so look for it [3].

cells: 12p gain in **46/87 (52.9%)** OGCT on CNA profiling: dysgerminoma 23/28 (82%), YST 11/19 (58%), mixed 10/23 (43%), **pure IT 0/15** (abstract: "all tumours except pure IT") [20]; 12p anomalies in **82%** (18/22) of dysgerminomas (FISH) [21]

Exon 17 codon 816 mutation **6/22 (27%)** and KIT amplification 6/22 (27%), not correlated; mutation associated with advanced stage (P = .045); KIT protein in 87% [21]. KIT codon 816 mutation in **5/14 unilateral dysgerminomas**, 0/4 bilateral, 0/22 other histotypes [11]. KIT mutated in 4/24 exomes, all dysgerminoma or mixed tumours with a dysgerminoma component [20]

PIK3CA amplification in 16/38 and AKT1 amplification in 14/38 YST-containing tumours; KRAS codon 12 mutation in 2/24 exomes (embryonal carcinoma; mixed YST–dysgerminoma) [20]. FoundationOne CDx in 10 OYST (1 failed): KRAS, KIT or ARID1A alterations in 3 of 9 profiled (reported as 33.3%); ARID1A alterations in 2 [22]

Average **0.05 mutations/Mb** (whole-exome, 24 OGCT) [20]; OYST median TMB **3 mut/Mb (range 0–5)**, **MSS in 9/9** [22]. MSI status may change at relapse (testicular case report), so test the recurrent sample [18]

Dysgerminoma **9/10**, YST **0/5**, IT 4/11, choriocarcinoma 2/2, mixed 5/5 (positive only in dysgerminoma and choriocarcinoma components); PD-L1 associated with CD8+ TILs (P = .003); no OS difference by PD-L1 status (P = .4); n = 34 [7]
TSPY expression and Y-chromosome material in 5 patients with dysgerminoma and/or gonadoblastoma (4 with bilateral neoplasia) [11]; worse EFS and OS in AGCT0132 (see Rare histotypes) [12]

Concurrent elevation of **both** β-hCG and AFP predicted OS in stage IC–IV MOGCT (multivariate **HR 3.90, 1.40–10.9**; stage HR 5.96, 3.47–10.2; called relative risks in the text) [23]. Paediatric model: stage IV, age ≥11 and site significant; AFP ≥10,000 ng/mL not significant (P = .45) [16]. TGM95 used AFP ≥15,000 ng/mL to define high risk [24]. All AGCT0132 stage I recurrences had raised AFP [13]
No LDH-specific MOGCT data in the sources retrieved

Stage IC–IV, cancer-specific survival (multivariable): non-dysgerminoma **HR 4.8 (1.7–16.9) vs dysgerminoma** and HR 7.3 (1.9–64.8) vs grade 2/3 IT (the abstract gives 7.3 as "nondysgerminoma"); age ≥35 HR 2.8 (1.4–5.4); advanced FIGO stage HR 1.4 (1.02–1.9). 10-yr CSS: grade 2/3 IT 97.5%, dysgerminoma 94.7%, mixed 77.8%, YST 71.7% [25]

mol.caption: **B. Treatment-selecting biomarkers.** Every row kept. None selects treatment in MOGCT.
columns: Assay / cutoff used in the pivotal trial
Existing regimens that select on it

cells: IHC loss of MLH1, PMS2, MSH2 or MSH6, or MSI-H by PCR/NGS
MSS 9/9 OYST [22]. Not a selection criterion in this histotype on current data
Endometrial templates only: EM Dostarlimab · EM Keytruda (no GCT template)

CPS not reported. Tumour-cell PD-L1 (22C3) >1%: dysgerminoma 9/10, YST 0/5, IT 4/11 [7]. Not a selection criterion in this histotype: no objective response to PD-1/PD-L1 blockade in GCT trials [26,27]
Cervical template only: CC Keytruda (no GCT template)
Not reported in the sources retrieved. Not a selection criterion in this histotype
Endometrial templates only: EM Enhertu · EM Herceptin
Germline or tumour BRCA1/2; myChoice GIS ≥42 (PAOLA-1)
HRD not reported; no BRCA1/2, ATM or RAD51C mutations in 24 OGCT exomes [20]; ARID1A alterations in 2 of 9 analysable OYST [22]. Not a selection criterion in this histotype
VENTANA FOLR1-2.1, **≥75% of viable tumour cells with ≥2+ membrane staining** (MIRASOL)
Not reported in the sources retrieved. Not a selection criterion in this histotype
*KIT (dysgerminoma), KRAS, PIK3CA/AKT1 amplification (YST); TMB-high and NTRK/RET/BRAF V600E not reported*

notes.title: Testing: AFP/β-hCG at diagnosis and follow-up [13,23]; check for gonadal dysgenesis [12]; genomic profiling only for refractory disease, on the recurrent sample [18,22].

sections.title: 1. Adjuvant / post-surgery early stage (stage I–II, completely resected): surveillance vs adjuvant chemotherapy

cols.regimen: VAC: vincristine 1.5 mg/m² weekly ×8–12 wk; dactinomycin 300 mcg/m² D1–5 and cyclophosphamide 150 mg/m² D1–5 q4w; ≥10 courses
cols.pop: Completely resected MOGCT (YST, embryonal, mixed, IT); children, adolescents and adults, age 7–56 (IT median 20 yr)
cols.hist: **MOGCT-only; histotype reported**: failure pure YST 11/24 (46%); mixed with YST 3/10 (30%); IT 1/20 (5%). `rare:` embryonal 2 (both incompletely resected, see T2)
cols.pfs: Failure **15/54 (28%)**; median time to progression 8 mo
cols.tox: Dose-limiting toxicity 30%; severe paresthesias or motor loss 23/27 (85%) with weekly vincristine. Stage I with uterus and contralateral ovary preserved: 21/28 (75%) resumed menses

cols.regimen: BEP ×3 after complete resection and staging (single arm): cisplatin 20 mg/m² D1–5, etoposide 100 mg/m² D1–5, bleomycin 30 U weekly, q21d
cols.pop: Completely resected, surgically staged stage I–III non-dysgerminomatous ovarian GCT (pure dysgerminoma ineligible); GOG cooperative group, age 11–53 yr (median 25)
cols.hist: **MOGCT-only**: IT 42, YST 25, mixed 24, choriocarcinoma 2; stage I 60, II 10, III 23
cols.pfs: **91/93 free of germ cell cancer** (89 continuously; 2 with small IT foci at second look); 2 clinical recurrences; follow-up 4.0–90.3 mo
cols.tox: AML 22 mo after diagnosis (1); lymphoma at 69 mo (1); no severe pulmonary toxicity, no drug-related deaths. Authors: BEP ×3 "should be given" to all such patients

cols.regimen: Surgery alone, no postoperative chemotherapy; surveillance
cols.pop: Completely resected stage I–II ovarian IT, **paediatric/adolescent**, age 1.5–20 yr
cols.n: 44 evaluable of 46 eligible (31 pure IT; 13 IT + microscopic YST foci)
cols.hist: **Paediatric ovarian IT only**; central pathology review; pure IT grade 1/2/3 = 17/12/2; AFP raised 10/29 pure IT, 10/12 IT + YST
cols.tox: The only relapse (IT + YST foci, at 18 weeks) was salvaged with PEB ×4; grade, rupture and gliomatosis did not predict outcome

cols.regimen: PEB ×4: cisplatin 20 mg/m² D1–5, etoposide 100 mg/m² D1–5, bleomycin 15 U/m² D1, q21d
cols.pop: **Paediatric** (8.7 mo–16.7 yr; girls ≤21 eligible) stage I–II ovarian (pure dysgerminoma ineligible) and stage II testicular MGCT
cols.hist: **Paediatric ovarian cohort reported by stage**; all 4 events in ovarian primaries
cols.pfs: 6-yr EFS ovarian stage I **95%** (abstract 95.1%), stage II **87.5%** (all 94.5%)
cols.tox: Grade 3–4 neutropenia 23%; no grade 3–4 renal, pulmonary or ototoxicity; secondary AML 2 (1 death). Ovarian staging guidelines followed in 1/56. Predates stage I surveillance

cols.regimen: Carboplatin 400 mg/m² D1 + etoposide 120 mg/m² D1–3, q4w ×3
cols.pop: Completely resected stage IB–III **dysgerminoma** (GOG cooperative group; age range not reported: <10 yr 1, 10–30 yr 27, >30 yr 11; stage II–III 54%)
cols.pfs: **No dysgerminoma recurrence (0/39)**; median follow-up 7.6 yr (abstract 7.8 yr)
cols.tox: Grade 3–4 neutropenia 31, no treatment-related deaths. One patient excluded on review (YST elements) died (abstract: of recurrent tumour). Closed before target accrual. Alternative to BEP when neuropathy or treatment days matter (no NTUH template)

cols.regimen: Surgery → surveillance (markers + imaging); compressed PEB ×3 at relapse (cisplatin 33.3 mg/m² D1–3, etoposide 167 mg/m² D1–3, bleomycin 15 U/m² D1)
cols.pop: **Girls 0–16 yr**, stage I MOGCT containing YST, embryonal carcinoma or choriocarcinoma
cols.hist: **Paediatric ovarian, non-dysgerminoma**; predominantly YST; AFP raised in 23. `rare:` embryonal, choriocarcinoma eligible
cols.pfs: 4-yr EFS **52% (31–69%)**; 12 persistent/recurrent, median time to recurrence 2 mo
cols.tox: ~50% spared chemotherapy; all recurrences AFP-positive

cols.regimen: Surveillance after complete surgical staging (chemotherapy in 14)
cols.pop: Stage I MOGCT, post-pubertal, conservatively treated, Italy; age 14–45 (mean 26.3)
cols.n: 45 (31 surveillance alone; 2 of 47 excluded after positive restaging)
cols.hist: **MOGCT-only**: group A (IA dysgerminoma, IA G1 IT) 13; group B (IB–C dysgerminoma, IA–C G2–3 IT, IA mixed or YST) 29; group C (IC YST or mixed) 5
cols.pfs: **1/31 relapse on surveillance** (3.2%; stage IA dysgerminoma at 26 mo, salvaged with BEP); none in groups B or C; 5-yr DFS 95% surveillance vs 100% chemotherapy; median follow-up 53.5 mo (abstract 46.2)
cols.tox: Prospective observational, small; restaging upstaged 2/6 incompletely staged group B patients

cols.regimen: Low risk (FIGO IA): no adjuvant therapy; IR: VBP ×3–5; HR: VIP ×4–6
cols.pfs: Low risk (surveillance): relapse/progression **6/14 (43%)**, 5 durable CR after salvage; FIGO IA 5-yr EFS 66.7% (42–85%); whole cohort 5-yr EFS 88.2% (79–94%); all relapses within 2 yr (abstract "6 LR, 1 IR"; results count 8 relapses/progressions)
cols.os: 5-yr OS 94.6% (87–98%); low-risk deaths 2 (HDCT toxicity 1, secondary AML 1)
cols.tox: See T2 for late effects

cols.regimen: *Surgery and staging → intensive surveillance*
cols.pop: *Stage I female GCT (ovary 35, other sites 2), median age 26 (14–48)*
cols.pfs: *Relapse stage IA non-dysgerminoma **8/22 (36%)**, dysgerminoma 2/9 (22%); all within 13 mo; 1-yr relapse-free 72%*
cols.os: *Disease-specific survival 93% (28/30 malignant stage IA; abstract 94%); 10/11 relapses cured with platinum chemotherapy*
cols.tox: *15 women had successful pregnancies after fertility-sparing surgery (54% as printed), 5 of them after relapse chemotherapy*

cols.regimen: *Surgery alone (90/98 paediatric) vs postoperative chemotherapy (all adults, GOG 0078/0090)*
cols.pop: *Pure ovarian IT from INT-0106, GC2, GOG 0078, GOG 0090; paediatric (age 0–17) and adult (age 11–49) cohorts analysed separately*
cols.pfs: *5-yr EFS paediatric 91%, adult 87%; **no relapses in grade 1**; grade 3 EFS paediatric stage I/II 0.92 vs III 0.52 (P = .005); adult I/II 0.91 vs III/IV 0.65 (P = .01)*
cols.hr: *Prognostic (adult, multivariable relative-risk regression): grade 3 vs 1/2 8.22 (1.01–67.13); stage III vs I/II 6.76 (1.36–33.67)*
cols.tox: *Grade 3 relapse 8/38 paediatric, 9/45 adult. Chemotherapy did not decrease relapses in the paediatric cohort (events 3/8 with vs 6/90 without, confounded by risk); role in adults unresolved*

cols.regimen: *Fertility-sparing surgery alone → surveillance*
cols.pfs: *10-yr DFS 77% (IA 77% vs IC 76%); recurrence 7 (22.6%), 6/7 salvaged with surgery + BEP*
cols.tox: *Median follow-up 137 mo*

cols.regimen: *Surgery + BEP ×3–4 (50.7%) vs surgery alone (49.3%)*
cols.pfs: *Recurrence 23 (16.0%); incomplete peritoneal staging the only independent risk factor (recurrence 26% vs 8.6%; Cox P = 0.04, estimate printed as OR 2.37, 1.04–5.44)*
cols.os: *5-yr OS standard 93.8% vs surveillance 94.1%; staged 96.8% vs incompletely staged 88.7% (NS); YST/mixed 83.7% vs other histotypes 98.6% (P < 0.05)*
cols.tox: *YST component the only independent factor for OS; 44 did not receive indicated chemotherapy, 35 of whom never needed it; 1 AML death after BEP*

cols.regimen: *Neoadjuvant/adjuvant chemotherapy (82% BEP) vs none*
cols.pop: *Ovarian GCT all stages, paediatric (≤18) and adult (>18 yr), median age 23.5 (8–76); relapse/progression rate 28% in both age groups (log-rank P = 0.96; the abstract prints these event rates as "EFS")*
cols.hist: ***Histotype-level, uncontrolled***: relapse/progression with vs without chemotherapy — dysgerminoma 0% vs 20% (n = 37); YST 26.3% vs 75% (n = 23); mixed 40% vs 70% (n = 30; abstract n = 32); **IT 33% vs 15% (n = 42)**
cols.tox: *27 potentially chronic toxicities; 1 death from ALL. No radiological response of IT to chemotherapy; IT grade did not predict EFS (univariable HR 0.82, 0.57–1.19; Cox P = 0.28, log-rank P = 0.94). Age ≥40: EFS HR 3.30 (1.26–8.67), OS 55%*

cols.regimen: *Adjuvant chemotherapy vs surveillance*
cols.pop: *FIGO IA/IB G2–3 IT, YST or mixed GCT, US 2004–2014; median age 23 (range not reported)*
cols.hist: ***Histotype-level registry, uncontrolled***: G2 IT 115, G3 IT 157, YST 101, mixed 124
cols.os: *No OS difference for G2/3 IT combined (5-yr 97.3% vs 95%, P = 0.22), G2 IT (P = 0.35), G3 IT (P = 0.47), mixed (P = 0.55); **YST 5-yr OS 92.7% with vs 79.6% without chemotherapy (P = 0.019)***
cols.tox: *Adjuvant chemotherapy 340/497 (68.4%; the abstract's "68.2% (655 patients)" is impossible for n = 497). Deaths 10/157 surveillance vs 9/340 chemotherapy; unadjusted analysis*

cols.regimen: *Postoperative chemotherapy (Brazil TCG-99/TCG-2008; 87% of stage II–IV) vs surgery alone (US/UK INT-0106/GC-2; 13% of stage II–IV given chemotherapy)*
cols.pfs: *Stage I EFS 88% vs 98% (p = .054); stage II–IV EFS 66% vs 79% (p = .32); grade 3 EFS 76% vs 78% (p = .85)*
cols.tox: *Chemotherapy did not improve outcome; the only Brazilian death was chemotherapy-related. Local file is the peer-review manuscript (published abstract: p = .05, 67%, p = .44)*

cols.regimen: Active surveillance for low-risk GCT
cols.tox: Rationale in [17]

notes.title: Reading Table 1
notes.md:
- **No randomized surveillance-vs-chemotherapy trial.** Surveillance trades relapse for chemo avoided; salvage preserves OS (paediatric EFS 52%, OS 96%) [13].
- **IT**: chemotherapy looks least useful [14,19,36]. **YST**: omitting it looks most costly (NCDB OS 92.7% vs 79.6%) [35]. Both uncontrolled.

sections.title: 2. Primary chemotherapy for advanced or incompletely resected disease (FIGO II–IV; paediatric intermediate/high risk)

cols.regimen: HDPEB (cisplatin **40** mg/m² D1–5) vs PEB (cisplatin 20 mg/m² D1–5); both etoposide 100 mg/m² D1–5, bleomycin 15 U/m² D1; ×4
cols.pop: **Paediatric/adolescent** (age ≤21) high-risk MGCT: stage III–IV gonadal, extragonadal all stages
cols.hist: **Paediatric ovarian cohort reported, arms combined** (by arm not reported): stage III 58, IV 16, age 1.4–20.1; 6-yr EFS 94.5% (stage III 96.6%, IV 86.7%), OS 97.3%
cols.orr: Week-12 CR 58.2% vs 51.4% (P = .15); CR + PR 96% in both arms
cols.tox: Toxic deaths 6 vs 1; tumour deaths 2 vs 14; grade 3–4 objective hearing loss 14% vs 0%; other toxicities more common with HDPEB, which limits its use

cols.regimen: PVB ×3–4 (GOG 45, n = 8) or BEP ×3 → VAC ×3 (GOG 90, n = 12): cisplatin 20 mg/m² D1–5, etoposide 100 mg/m² D1–5, bleomycin 20 U/m² weekly
cols.pop: Advanced (III, IV, recurrent) incompletely resected **dysgerminoma** unsuitable for radiotherapy; central pathology review (age range ⬜)
cols.pfs: **19/20 (95%) disease-free**, median follow-up 26 mo; second look negative 14/14
cols.tox: No clinically apparent bleomycin lung, no drug-related deaths. Authors recommend BEP ×3 without VAC consolidation

cols.regimen: PVB ×3–4: cisplatin 20 mg/m² D1–5, vinblastine 12 mg/m² D1, bleomycin 20 U/m² weekly; salvage VAC or EP
cols.pop: Stage II–IV or recurrent MOGCT with residual disease; age <20 in 43%
cols.hist: **MOGCT-only; histotype reported**: disease-free YST 16/29 (55%), mixed 14/27 (52%), IT 14/26 (54%). `rare:` embryonal 1/4, choriocarcinoma 2/3
cols.tox: Treatment-related deaths 5 (2 pulmonary fibrosis, 2 myelosuppression with infection, 1 sudden); dose modification 49%. Measurable (P = 0.002) and recurrent (P = 0.015) disease predicted failure

cols.regimen: VAC (as T1)
cols.hist: **MOGCT-only**: mixed with YST 5/5 failed. `rare:` embryonal 2/2 failed
cols.tox: Established that VAC is inadequate for residual disease

cols.regimen: JEb: carboplatin 600 mg/m² D2, etoposide 120 mg/m² D1–3, bleomycin 15 mg/m² D3; q3–4w until remission + 2 courses
cols.pop: **Children <16 yr**, malignant extracranial GCT (all sites); watch-and-wait after complete excision of stage I testicular and some ovarian
cols.hist: **Included; ovarian subgroup reported**: ovarian JEb 5-yr EFS **90.7% (78.2–96.4%)**; ovarian 5-yr OS 92.3% (79.0–97.5%, all 54); 3/9 ovarian watch-and-wait recurrences, all salvaged with JEb. `rare:` embryonal 1, choriocarcinoma 1 (both ovarian)
cols.tox: Grade 3 deafness 1, no significant renal toxicity; 1 treatment-related death and 1 secondary AML death. Median 5 courses. AFP ≥10,000 kU/L an independent adverse factor

cols.regimen: PEb ×3, compressed to 3 days per cycle (cisplatin 33.3 mg/m² and etoposide 167 mg/m² D1–3, bleomycin 15 U/m² D1)
cols.pop: **Children/adolescents** (median age 11), intermediate-risk MGCT: stage II–III ovarian, II–IV testicular, I–II extragonadal, relapsed stage I gonadal
cols.hist: **Included; ovarian subgroup reported**: ovary n = 124, 4-yr EFS 88% (80–92%); stage II 90%, stage III 85% (historical 4 cycles 88% and 95%)
cols.pfs: 4-yr EFS **89% (83–92%)**, below the 92% threshold (P = .08); stage I 100%, II 92%, III 85%, IV (testicular only) 54%
cols.hr: vs historical PEb ×4: 0.61 (0.26–1.42), P = .24 (reference arm ambiguous as printed)
cols.tox: Newly diagnosed 87% vs 92% historical 4-cycle cohort (P = .15). Grade 3–4 neutropenia 50%. Authors: do not reduce 4 → 3 cycles

cols.regimen: IR (IC–III, AFP <15,000): VBP ×3–5; HR (metastatic or AFP ≥15,000): VIP ×4–6
cols.hist: **Paediatric ovarian cohort**: IR 2 malignant progressions/26; HR 0 relapses/37
cols.tox: Chronic kidney disease 4 of 40 evaluated (abstract "three after VIP"; results describe 2 VIP-exposed); clinically significant ototoxicity 3 of 37 evaluated (Brock grade 2 ×2, tinnitus 1); 2 AML deaths; 4 contralateral mature teratomas

cols.regimen: *BEP (etoposide D1–3, cisplatin 100 mg/m² D1, q4w)*
cols.pop: *MOGCT age 8–32 (median 19); stage I–III and recurrent; residual >2 cm in 3*
cols.tox: *Second look negative 4/4; no drug-related deaths; severe neutropenia 5*

cols.regimen: *PVB 9, BEP 15, **BEC (carboplatin) 25***
cols.pop: *MOGCT after initial surgery, age 12–69 (median 20); complete resection 40%*
cols.pfs: *Progression-free: dysgerminoma 13/13; non-dysgerminoma 34/40 (85%), incompletely resected 17/21 (80% as printed)*
cols.tox: *1 death from bleomycin lung toxicity; no difference by cisplatin vs carboplatin (data not shown)*

cols.regimen: *POMB/ACE 89, BEP 17 (stage IC/M–II with low markers), other regimens 7*
cols.os: *10-yr OS 81%; 5-yr OS stage IC/M 100%, II 85%, III 79%, IV 71%*
cols.hr: *Prognostic OS (multivariate; HR in table, relative risk in text): stage 5.96 (3.47–10.2); both β-hCG and AFP raised 3.90 (1.40–10.9)*
cols.tox: *20 relapses, all within 8 yr; long-term control after relapse 2/20; age not prognostic*

cols.regimen: *Adjuvant chemotherapy in 65.9% (BEP 70/81)*
cols.hist: ***MOGCT-only, uncontrolled***: dysgerminoma 49, IT 35, YST 26, mixed 12. `rare:` embryonal 1
cols.tox: *Age >45 and treatment outside a referral centre predicted recurrence; stage >I and YST predicted death (relative risks); YST relapses not salvaged (0/5)*

cols.regimen: *Cisplatin era (after 1980) vs before*
cols.tox: *Second cancer in 23/139 10-yr survivors after cytotoxic treatment vs 0/31 surgery only (Fisher P = 0.05; log-rank P = 0.08)*

cols.regimen: *Carboplatin-based JEB (CCLG, UK; carboplatin 600 mg/m²) vs cisplatin-based PEb (COG; including HD-PEb and C-PEb)*
cols.pop: *Paediatric/adolescent extracranial MGCT trials since 1983 (upper age 15 yr CCLG, 21 yr most COG)*
cols.hist: ***Paediatric ovarian subgroup reported***, uncontrolled cross-trial: ovarian (n = 278) 4-yr EFS 85% vs 90% (p = 0.38)
cols.pfs: *4-yr EFS **86% (79–90%) vs 86% (83–89%)**, p = 0.87; no difference by site, stage, age or risk group*
cols.tox: *Equipoise for AGCT1531 randomization*

cols.regimen: *BEP 122, POMB/ACE 108, other platinum-based 24; surgery first in 87.8% (remainder neoadjuvant chemotherapy)*
cols.pop: ***Adults**, stage IC–IV MOGCT, UK + MITO, 1971–2018, median age 27*
cols.hist: ***MOGCT-only, uncontrolled***: 10-yr CSS grade 2/3 IT 97.5% mirrored dysgerminoma 94.7%; YST 71.7%, mixed 77.8%
cols.os: *10-yr CSS 83.2% (77.3–87.7%); stage IV 79.4% (61.5–89.7%; the abstract prints the stage III CI, 69.5–86.4)*
cols.hr: *Prognostic CSS (multivariable): non-dysgerminoma vs dysgerminoma 4.8 (1.7–16.9), vs grade 2/3 IT 7.3 (1.9–64.8); age ≥35 2.8 (1.4–5.4); advanced stage 1.4 (1.02–1.9). POMB/ACE vs BEP 1.4 (0.7–2.9), NS*
cols.tox: *37 (14.5%) died of disease; 7 (2.8%) treatment-related deaths*

cols.regimen: EP ×3 vs BEP ×3 (cisplatin 20 mg/m² D1–5, etoposide 100 mg/m² D1–5 ± bleomycin 30 IU weekly)
cols.tox: Unfavourable outcomes 38% vs 17% (P = .004); omitting bleomycin with 3 cycles worse; no clinically significant pulmonary toxicity with bleomycin

cols.regimen: CEB (carboplatin AUC-based, target 5 mg/mL·min) vs BEP ×4 (etoposide 120 mg/m² D1–3, bleomycin 30 U D2)
cols.tox: Carboplatin inferior at these doses, not explained by underdosing; conflicts with the paediatric MaGIC equivalence (see warning)

cols.regimen: BEP ×3 vs ×4; 5-day vs 3-day (etoposide 500 mg/m² per cycle)
cols.tox: Equivalence claimed; less sensory neuropathy and better quality of life at 3 months with 3 cycles. Basis for BEP ×3

cols.regimen: *BEP (good prognosis) vs POMB-ACE (intermediate/poor), non-randomized*
cols.tox: *Neutropenic sepsis POMB-ACE 22 (46%) vs BEP 5 (4%); bleomycin pulmonary toxicity BEP 4 (3%)*

cols.regimen: Randomized carboplatin- vs cisplatin-based bleomycin–etoposide (standard risk)
cols.tox: Designed on the MaGIC equipoise [17]

notes.title: Traps in Table 2
notes.md:
- **Carboplatin:** equal to cisplatin in children (EFS 86% vs 86%) [17] but inferior in adult men (3-yr OS 90% vs 97%) [46]. No adult-female data; AGCT1531 pending.
- **Don't drop cycles or bleomycin:** compressed PEb ×3 missed its target [40]; EP ×3 < BEP ×3 [45].

notes.title: Trial dosing vs NTUH templates
notes.md:
- **BEP:** trials give etoposide 100 mg/m² D1–5 (500/cycle) [38,47]; the NTUH template gives D1–3 (300/cycle). Check before use.
- **EP:** NTUH template (cisplatin 80 + etoposide 80 D1–3 ×2) is not a trial-matched GCT regimen [45].
- **GOG-116 carboplatin–etoposide:** no NTUH template [30].

sections.title: 3. Recurrent disease
sections.intro: Split by **GCT platinum sensitivity**: **3A** relapse >4–6 weeks after platinum; **3B** refractory or multiply relapsed, incl. post-HDCT [18].

notes.title: Mostly male data. Recurrence is uncommon (17.8%) [43] and salvage is poor (10% long-term survival) [23]; no ovarian GCT has responded to a checkpoint inhibitor [18].

sections.title: 3A. Platinum-sensitive / first relapse (relapse >4–6 weeks after platinum)

cols.regimen: PVB ×3–4
cols.tox: Recurrent status independently predicted failure (P = 0.015). Cisplatin-naive recurrence — not a post-platinum salvage estimate

cols.regimen: *Tandem high-dose carboplatin 700 mg/m² + etoposide 750 mg/m² D1–3, ×2 courses with stem-cell rescue (1 VeIP cycle first when initial salvage of platinum-sensitive disease)*
cols.pop: *Cisplatin-based; HDCT second line 5, third line 5, fourth or fifth line 3*
cols.hist: ***MOGCT-only, uncontrolled*** (correspondence): YST 11, non-gestational choriocarcinoma 2. `rare:` choriocarcinoma 0/2 long-term survivors
cols.pfs: *Continuously NED 4/13 (12–270+ mo); platinum-sensitive 3/5 vs refractory 1/8; second line 3/5 vs later 1/8*
cols.tox: *No treatment-related deaths; neutropenic fever 8, grade 3–4 mucositis 5; second course omitted for toxicity in 2*

rows.name: International adult cohort, HDCT at relapse

cols.regimen: *Tandem high-dose chemotherapy (HDCT) with stem-cell support vs conventional salvage (TIP-type regimens) ± surgery*
cols.n: *254; 40 given second-line or later treatment, HDCT in 13 (32.5%)*
cols.pfi: *First (n = 10) vs later (n = 3) relapse; PFI not reported*
cols.pfs: *HDCT at second line: PFS 80%, 60% and 45% at 1, 2 and 5 yr; HDCT 2-yr PFS 50% after an initial CR vs 20% after SD/PD*
cols.os: *5-yr CSS: HDCT 34.2%, conventional chemotherapy 25.0%, chemotherapy + surgery 29.0%; all 3 given HDCT at later relapse died of disease*
cols.hr: *CSS, HDCT vs conventional chemotherapy 0.16 (0.04–0.68), P = .013 (univariable table, teratomas excluded: 0.23, 0.07–0.73)*
cols.tox: *Supports HDCT at first relapse; not randomized, few events*

cols.regimen: Cisplatin + ifosfamide + etoposide or vinblastine (PEI/VeIP) ×4 vs ×3 → one cycle of high-dose carboplatin, etoposide, cyclophosphamide (CarboPEC) + stem cells
cols.pfi: Relapse after CR or PR to first-line platinum; refractory disease (progression within 1 month) excluded
cols.os: 3-yr OS 53% (46–59%), no significant difference (2-yr 57% vs 56%, P = 0.92)
cols.orr: CR + PR 56% (both arms); overall CR 42% vs 43%
cols.tox: Toxic deaths 3% vs 7%. Single HDCT cycle after 3 conventional cycles did not improve outcome

cols.regimen: TIP ×4: paclitaxel **250** mg/m² 24-h D1, ifosfamide 1500 mg/m² D2–5, cisplatin 25 mg/m² D2–5, mesna, G-CSF
cols.pop: ≤6 cycles of one cisplatin programme; prior CR/PR with negative markers
cols.pfi: >6 mo after first-line (favourable selection); testis primary
cols.tox: Neutropenic-fever admissions 22 patients (48%); grade 4–5 renal 3 (7%); 1 treatment-related death

cols.regimen: TIP ×4: paclitaxel **175** mg/m² (3 h) D1, ifosfamide 1 g/m² D1–5, cisplatin 20 mg/m² D1–5, q3w
cols.tox: Granulocytopenic fever 28%; 1 toxic death. Inferior to the intensive MSKCC schedule

cols.regimen: VeIP ×4: vinblastine 0.11 mg/kg D1–2, ifosfamide 1.2 g/m² D1–5, cisplatin 20 mg/m² D1–5
cols.hist: **⚠️ extrapolated (male GCT)**; 1 ovarian dysgerminoma, continuously disease-free
cols.tox: No extragonadal nonseminoma cured (0/32); neutropenic-fever admission 71% (no G-CSF); 3 drug-related deaths

cols.regimen: *HDCT (carboplatin-based) vs conventional-dose cisplatin-based first salvage*
cols.hr: ***OS 0.65 (0.56–0.75); PFS 0.44 (0.39–0.51)**, favouring HDCT, stratified by prognostic category*
cols.tox: *No OS difference in low-risk category (HR 1.0); sequential better than single-cycle HDCT*

cols.regimen: *Carboplatin 700 mg/m² + etoposide 750 mg/m² ×3 days, ×2 courses, each with PBSC rescue (VeIP cytoreduction in 110)*
cols.pfs: *116/184 (63%) continuously disease-free (median follow-up 48 mo); second-line **94/135**; platinum-sensitive 98/144*
cols.hr: *Prognostic (progression, multivariate): third-line or later 2.19 (1.35–3.56); platinum-refractory 1.74 (1.01–3.00); IGCCCG high risk 1.67 (1.00–2.78)*
cols.tox: *3 drug-related deaths; 3 secondary leukaemias*

cols.regimen: *TIP*
cols.pfi: *First salvage; 10 for a second gonadal primary*
cols.tox: *Median follow-up 8.9 yr*

cols.regimen: TIP (conventional dose) vs sequential high-dose TI-CE
cols.hist: Ongoing / design; men >16 yr after 3–6 cycles of first-line cisplatin [57]
cols.tox: No PubMed results publication found (2026-09-15); cited as determining second-line approach [56]

cols.regimen: Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w
cols.hist: **Included, 2 ovarian cases**: mixed IT grade 2/YST/embryonal (PD-L1 H-score 0), PFS 4.1 mo, OS 7.4 mo; YST with hepatic involvement, PFS 2.5 mo, OS 4.6 mo; both progressed. `rare:` embryonal component
cols.tox: 27-week non-progression 9.0% (primary endpoint >20% not met). Grade 3 immune pneumonitis 1

cols.regimen: *Salvage surgery + chemotherapy*
cols.hist: ***MOGCT-only, uncontrolled***: IT 19, YST 26, mixed 13, dysgerminoma 1; age 1–39
cols.tox: *Second relapse 19 (32.2%); death 16 (27.1%). Optimal salvage surgery and regimen independently prognostic. PFI not reported*

cols.regimen: *Single-cycle high-dose carboplatin 600 mg/m² + etoposide 600 mg/m² D1–3 + autologous stem-cell transplant, after TIP induction*
cols.pop: *≥1 platinum line; 2 prior lines 14, 3 lines 5, ≥4 lines 2*
cols.hist: ***MOGCT-only, uncontrolled***; relapsed and refractory not separated; YST 8, mixed 5, non-gestational choriocarcinoma 4, dysgerminoma 2, IT 2. `rare:` choriocarcinoma 4
cols.os: *Median 14.8 mo; median follow-up 51.7 mo; 7/21 alive without disease*
cols.tox: *Transplant-related mortality 1 (4.8%); fewer prior lines and CR before HDCT associated with longer PFS/OS (univariable)*

cols.regimen: Gemcitabine 800 mg/m² D1, D8 + paclitaxel 80 mg/m² D1, D8 + oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² D1, q3w
cols.pop: Median 2 platinum lines; 78% prior HDCT; 73% relapsed within 3 mo of cisplatin
cols.pfs: Median PFS 3 mo (1–17+); 15% in CR after GOP ± resection (median follow-up 5 mo); median response duration 8 mo
cols.tox: Grade 3/4 thrombocytopenia 49%, leukopenia 15%; no toxic deaths

cols.regimen: Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w
cols.tox: 6 grade 3 AEs; no immune-related AEs. PD-L1 positive in 2 (non-responders)

cols.regimen: *As 3A*
cols.pop: *Refractory to standard-dose platinum; third-line or later*
cols.tox: *Cure possible even when platinum-refractory*

notes.title: Reading Table 3
notes.md:
- **Ovarian salvage data = small retrospective series** [25,49,58,59]; HDCT at first relapse looked best in adults (CSS HR 0.16) [25].
- **HDCT vs conventional salvage is unresolved even in men** [50,54]; TIGER unreported.
- **Checkpoint inhibitors: 0% ORR** [26,27].

notes.title: Salvage dosing vs NTUH templates
notes.md:
- **TIP:** NTUH templates (paclitaxel 175 24-h, cisplatin 25 D2–5, ifosfamide 1200 D2–5, ×6) sit between MRC [52] and MSKCC [51]; trials gave 4 cycles, not 6.
- **GOP:** NTUH template matches the trial [60].

sections.title: 4. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy and fertility-sparing treatment
sections.intro: **No randomized data.** Table 4 is split: **4A** neoadjuvant chemotherapy for advanced disease; **4B** reproductive outcomes after fertility-sparing surgery with or without platinum chemotherapy.

cols.regimen: *BEP ×4 → fertility-sparing surgery (USO + omentectomy ± lymphadenectomy)*
cols.pop: *Stage III (20) or IV (3), bulky, ECOG 2–3, age 14–28*
cols.pfs: *CR 16, PR 5 to NACT; pathological CR 13/18 operated; estimated 10-yr DFS 87% (vs 69.5% upfront surgery)*
cols.os: ***21/23 alive and disease-free**, median follow-up 74 mo*
cols.fertility: *18/21 resumed menses; 10 women delivered 13 full-term babies*
cols.tox: *Comparator 43 upfront-surgery advanced patients (30 alive and disease-free); treatment group did not significantly affect DFS*

cols.regimen: *NACT → interval surgery vs primary debulking surgery*
cols.pop: *Stage III–IV YST or mixed with YST, median age 24 vs 23*
cols.fertility: *Fertility-sparing surgery 79.0% vs 81.0%; fertility outcomes not reported*
cols.tox: *NACT: all R0/R1; blood loss 328.4 vs 1285.7 mL (p = 0.029); peri-operative complications 15.8% vs 47.6% (p = 0.032); 1 post-operative death after PDS*

cols.regimen: *BEP-based NACT (EP for cycle 1 in 4) → surgery (fertility-sparing 18, complete 12)*
cols.pfs: *RECIST CR 5, PR 23 to NACT; pathological CR 15/30 (dysgerminoma 8/9); 7 progressed after adjuvant therapy (all YST or mixed)*
cols.os: *20/30 alive and disease-free; 5 deaths (4 progression, 1 bleomycin toxicity); median follow-up 42 mo*
cols.tox: *Stage, optimal surgery and viable tumour prognostic; dysgerminoma did better*

cols.regimen: *Surgery first in 87.8%; neoadjuvant chemotherapy in 31 (12.2%)*
cols.hr: *CSS, fertility-sparing surgery first vs chemotherapy first 0.6 (0.2–1.8); non-fertility-sparing surgery first vs chemotherapy first 1.3 (0.5–3.9); both NS*
cols.fertility: *Fertility-sparing surgery 50.4% of cohort; after NACT 16/31 (51.6%); fertility outcomes not measured*
cols.tox: *See T2*

sections.title: 4B. Fertility-sparing surgery ± platinum chemotherapy: reproductive outcomes

cols.regimen: *BEP after surgery (unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy in 16)*
cols.fertility: *Fertility-sparing: 13/14 (93%) returned to prechemotherapy menstrual pattern; 5 pregnancies; 2 had difficulty conceiving*
cols.tox: *1 apparent second primary in the remaining ovary, salvaged*

cols.regimen: *Surgery + platinum-based chemotherapy*
cols.pop: *Survivors ≥18 yr, disease-free ≥2 yr, vs matched controls*
cols.fertility: *Fertility-sparing 71 (53.8%): 62 (87.3%) still menstruating; premature menopause 2/71; 24 survivors reported 37 offspring*
cols.tox: *Greater reproductive concerns (P < .0001), less sexual pleasure (P = .017; abstract .003); better dyadic adjustment (P = .010)*

cols.regimen: *Uterine preservation vs hysterectomy (surgery + chemotherapy)*
cols.tox: *Hysterectomy group older and more often bilateral*

cols.regimen: *Fertility-sparing surgery alone vs + chemotherapy (POMB-ACE-type 39, BEP 10)*
cols.fertility: *Conception **85.7% vs 84.4%** (p = 1.0); live birth 80.4% (37/46); 5-yr live-birth probability 48% vs 40% (p = 0.55)*
cols.tox: *Cisplatin and cyclophosphamide doses did not differ by conception*

cols.regimen: *Fertility-sparing surgery ± chemotherapy (57.9%; mean 4.1 cycles)*
cols.fertility: *29/38 (76.3%) attempting pregnancy conceived; median menstrual recovery after BEP 5.6 mo; premature ovarian failure 1*
cols.tox: *Pregnancy desire was the only predictor of live birth*

notes.title: Reading Table 4 and late effects
notes.md:
- **NACT** enables fertility-sparing surgery in bulky disease; all uncontrolled [61,62].
- **Platinum rarely ends fertility**: conception 84.4% vs 85.7% [67].
- **Late effects**: bleomycin lung 6.8% (risk: GFR <80, >300,000 IU, age >40) [69]; ototoxicity [70,71]; second cancers after chemotherapy [28,29,44].
